_Original post on the nlmixr2 project blog is [here](https://blog.nlmixr2.org/blog/2026-10-11-nlmixr2save/)._

The nlmixr2 Working Group continues to expand what open source R tooling can support in pharmacometrics. In a new post, Matthew Fidler introduces `nlmixr2save` 0.2.0, now on CRAN. `saveFit()` writes a finished fit as text you can open later, and the `:=` operator caches a long run so a script or report does not fit the same model again.

A nonlinear mixed-effects fit can take minutes to weeks, and `saveRDS()` ties the result to R’s binary format and to how nlmixr2 stored the object internally. That tie already broke once, when compressed fits moved off the `qs` package. `saveFit()` splits the fit into nlmixr2 and rxode2 source plus CSV tables, bundled in one zip, and `loadFit()` rebuilds a working fit for diagnostic plots, VPCs, and the next model. While you are developing, changing `<-` to `:=` hashes the model, the data, and the estimation options, then loads the cache when nothing has changed. The post also covers cache options for a project or a rendered document, and `nlmixr2saveShare()` for sharing a model when the subject-level data has to stay behind. The same material is on the nlmixr2save poster at ACoP 2026 (October 11–14, National Harbor, Maryland).

Watch the 7-minute narrated walkthrough: [https://youtu.be/TD7yhaaQToE](https://youtu.be/TD7yhaaQToE)

Read the full post from the nlmixr2 blog: [nlmixr2save: fits you can read, runs you don't repeat](https://blog.nlmixr2.org/blog/2026-10-11-nlmixr2save/)

## Why nlmixr2?

The vision of nlmixr2 is to develop a R-based open source nonlinear mixed-effects modeling software package that can compete with commercial pharmacometric tools and is suitable for regulatory submissions.

In short, the goal of nlmixr2 is to support easy and robust nonlinear mixed effects models in R.

From: [https://github.com/nlmixr2/nlmixr2](https://github.com/nlmixr2/nlmixr2)
